resources.string: Choose a photo to add an inset information card. Your original stays unchanged.
Blank fields are hidden. Photo GPS and known lens metadata are filled automatically when available. All fields remain editable; set the default photographer in Settings.
Pixel values refer to an 859 px short edge. Photo orientation and export resolution scale the card consistently.
100% matches the reference text. Text always scales with the photo; increasing this setting keeps the card width and adds height only when needed.
The default card font is included in this build when available. Imported fonts stay in private app storage; Reset restores the default.
Rendering the original photo. Keep the app open.
Output: 8-bit sRGB SDR. HDR gain maps, Live Photo video and RAW data are not preserved. A new image is saved; the original is untouched.
The card is taller than the photo. Reduce card scale or shorten the text. No text has been truncated.
There is not enough memory for this photo. Close other apps or choose a smaller image. Export resolution has not been reduced.
Saved for future imports when EXIF has no photographer. Editing one photo does not change this default.
Save and apply to current photo
Resolve photo GPS to a place

Sends photo coordinates to the Android system place-name service, which may use the network. It does not read your current location or upload the photo. English city and country names are requested. Exported EXIF still excludes GPS.
Known profiles include Xiaomi 17 Ultra and Xiaomi 14. For other devices, an explicit zoom in LensModel is preferred; optionally set the equivalent focal length of the 1× main camera below.
Optional. Applies to future imports from unknown devices. Leave blank to show focal length only when zoom is unknown.
Enter a number from 1 to 200, or leave blank.
Resolving photo location… You can keep editing.
Place resolved from photo GPS. You can edit it.
No place returned. Check the network, retry, or enter it manually.
No readable GPS in this photo. Try importing the original from Files, or enter a place manually.
Automatic place lookup is off in Settings.
Uses the photo GPS, not your current location.
